request.spec:
A steward can assign a REVIEW claim to a user (an entry and a button on the claim;
REVIEW_ASSIGNED naming the claim and ending user=<user>; a blank user, any other status or anyone
else is refused). The claim shows the assigned user, and the header shows the signed-in user the
count of REVIEW claims assigned to them.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can assign a REVIEW claim to a user (an entry and a button on the claim;
REVIEW_ASSIGNED naming the claim and ending user=<user>; a blank user, any other status or anyone
else is refused). The claim shows the assigned user, and the header shows the signed-in user the
count of REVIEW claims assigned to them.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Review assignment is in, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass. One of them only passed after I also fixed an older bug in bulk settle (below).

**What's new**
- **On each claim:** a user entry (`claim-review-user`), an "Assign review" button (`claim-review-assign`) and the assigned user (`claim-review-assigned`). The server takes the request at `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/assign-review`. It refuses anyone but a steward, a blank user and any claim not in REVIEW. A refusal shows `claim-error`, stores nothing and writes no audit line.
- **Delegation:** a user a steward has delegated to can assign too. Their audit line gets ` for=<steward>` added at the end, the same way as other delegated changes.
- **Audit line:** `REVIEW_ASSIGNED sheet=… by=… person=… amount=… date=… user=<user>`.
- **Stored data:** a new `review_user` column on claims, added in migration `V94__claim_review_user.sql` and also kept in the claim history table. It's carried along when a person is transferred to another sheet.
- **Header:** `my-reviews-count` shows how many REVIEW claims are assigned to the signed-in user. A claim that leaves REVIEW still shows who it was assigned to, but stops counting.

**Change outside the request.** The fourth test failed at first on `bulk-settle-batch`. The number shown there was worked out from the claims on the sheet. After a person was transferred away, no claim carried the batch, so it went blank, while the test expects it to stay "1". I added `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/last-batch`, which reads the sheet's own batch counter, and `features/claims/settle.slot.tsx` now shows that number. When you view the sheet as of a past date, it still shows the batch from the claims at that time.
